chunks: And with his chain of narration, he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
You, O Ali, are in Paradise, and you are the one who holds its two ends.

key_terms.ذُو قَرْنَيْهَا: Holder of its two ends (referring to Paradise)

ai.seo_question: What does the title 'Dhu al-Qarnayn' or 'holder of the two ends' mean for Imam Ali in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights Ali ibn Abi Talib's unique eschatological status, where the title 'Dhu al-Qarnayn' (Possessor of the Two Horns/Ends) is interpreted by Shia scholars as denoting his comprehensive authority over the entirety of Paradise, encompassing both its physical gates and spiritual realms. It serves as a key text for establishing the Imam's preeminence in the afterlife, linking his earthly leadership directly to his eternal reward.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-310 According to the same documentation, the Prophet (S) said,
“O Ali! You will be in Paradise and both ends of it are under your control.”
